steps.title: Game rules
steps.body: Logic makes a map a game: when something happens (an event), do something (actions). Here it decides what the chest holds: when the cinematic says “open-chest”, logic opens the lid, puts the item in the chest, lifts it out and gives it to the hero. Graph and code are two views of the same rules.

steps.title: A graph for the chest
steps.body: A graph holds rules: event chains that start with an event node (teal). + New makes one that starts with “On start”. Name graphs after what they are about, so you find them later.
steps.task: Make a new graph named “Treasure chest”.

how.text: In the panel on the left, next to “Graphs”, click “+ New”. A graph “Logic …” opens with an “On start” node.
At the top of the editor, click the graph’s name, select it, type Treasure chest and press Enter.

do.say: Type Treasure chest as the graph’s name and press Enter.

steps.title: The chest’s item is a variable
steps.body: Variables remember things while playing. Here “chestItem” holds the name of what is inside the chest. The rules read it instead of saying “Sword”, so changing this one value makes the same chest give anything (any asset by its name).
steps.task: Add a text variable “chestItem” that starts as Sword.

how.text: Under “Variables” (left), type chestItem in the box “New variable” and click “Add”. A row “chestItem” appears, a number starting at 0.
In that row, open the drop-down (it says “number”) and pick “text”.
In the row’s box (starts at), type Sword and press Enter. The chest will hold a Sword.

do.say: Type Sword in the row’s box and press Enter.

steps.title: Listen for the cinematic
steps.body: Events start a chain. “On custom event” runs when something sends that event’s name: a cinematic, an asset interaction, another graph. The scene you direct later sends “open-chest” at the moment Rowan lifts the lid.
steps.task: Add an “On custom event” node for the event “open-chest”.

how.text: Under “Nodes” (left), type custom in “Find a node”, then click “On custom event”. The node appears in the graph and is selected: its settings show on the right.

do.say: Click “On custom event”: it is added and selected.

how.text: On the right, open “Event name”, pick “＋ New event…”, type open-chest and press Enter.

do.say: Open “Event name” and pick “＋ New event…”.

steps.title: Open the lid
steps.body: “Set state” switches a placed asset to one of its states. Its target can be an id or an asset’s name: “Treasure chest” means the chest nearest the hero. The chest’s lid is a moving part: it swings open over 0.7 s. Wires carry the flow from a white “then” pin to a white “in” pin.
steps.task: Add “Set state” (Treasure chest → open) and wire “On custom event” then → its in.

how.text: Type set state in “Find a node” (left) and click “Set state”. It is added and selected.

do.say: Type set state in “Find a node”.

how.text: On the right under “Values”, in “target”, type Treasure chest and press Enter; “state” already says open.
In the graph, drag from the white “then” pin of “On custom event” to the white “in” pin of “Set state”. A wire joins them: when the event comes, the lid opens.

do.say: Drag from “then” on “On custom event” to “in” on “Set state”.

steps.title: The rest as code
steps.body: The same rules as code: each node is a line. Spawn item at object puts the item named in chestItem inside the chest; Set state “out” makes it rise (the Sword’s moving part); Give item puts it in the hero’s bag. A second event, “take-sword”, removes the floating sword when Rowan takes it. Split shows code and graph.
steps.task: Switch to Split and type the code; the graph grows with every line.

how.text: At the top of the editor, click “Split”: code on one side, the graph on the other.
In the code, below what is there, type the lines shown in the card (or select all the code and type them in its place). After a short pause the graph shows the new nodes and wires.

do.say: The code is typed; the graph follows.
